subject: RLHF throughput dip impacting BrightCart — triage, product asks & customer note
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29 08:12 -0700
Subject: [Alert] RLHF job class — throughput dip across GenAPI (BrightCart impacted)

Team,

Datadog alerted at 08:05 PST for sustained throughput drop (~35%) on the RLHF job class for GenAPI endpoints. Affected customers identified via routing metadata: BrightCart (high traffic), two internal test accounts. P95/99 for token generation pushed up ~2-3x for ~20 minutes before partial recovery; however BrightCart is still seeing elevated tails.

What I’ve collected so far:
- snapshot (csv) attached: rlhf-throughput-snapshot-20260829.csv
- initial hypothesis: a kernel scheduling change that rolled yesterday evening (candidate: kernel scheduling v3 -> v4) is increasing context-switch overhead on long-seq RLHF runs
- quick mitigation attempted: increased concurrency cap for RLHF pool (small improvement, not back to baseline)

Ask: can ENG/SRE triage root cause and scope rollback/backout options? Product (Marcus/Marissa) — please flag any customer messaging constraints (SLA/credit guidance). I started an incident in INC-2345.

Ben
SRE Manager

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: [Alert] RLHF job class — throughput dip across GenAPI (BrightCart impacted)

Thanks Ben — reading the snapshot now. A couple quick technical questions for triage:

1) Are the affected instances all on the kernel-sched v4 rollout? If yes, can we roll back just the canary subset and compare?
2) Any correlation with sequence-length distribution changes from BrightCart? If they pushed longer prompts, that could amplify scheduling contention.

Product note: if kernel rollback helps, we should consider pausing the v4 rollout and add a canary gate tied to 95/99 latency for RLHF-type workloads. That should be a roadmap item but needs an exception now.

I can spare time to pair with Ben for an immediate rollback test. Marcus
Principal Product Manager — Serving Runtime

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29 10:02 -0700
Subject: Update: targeted rollback applied; early signal of improvement

Quick update from the runbook steps:
- At 09:10 PST we rolled kernel-sched v3 back onto a 12% canary of RLHF-serving hosts in the affected cohort.
- Within 6 minutes those hosts showed p50/p95/p99 improvements (attached png). Overall cluster throughput improved ~18% and BrightCart p99 dropped from ~1.8s -> ~0.9s on the canary slice.
- We then expanded rollback to the remaining impacted hosts on the same cluster at 09:38 PST.
- By 09:50 PST BrightCart metrics are within normal bounds; Datadog shows p99 back to baseline.

Mitigation complete; I’m keeping the temporary routing rule in place for 2 hours while we monitor. Next steps:
- Post-incident RCA (INC-2345) to confirm root cause and whether kernel-sched v4 needs a rework.
- Marcus/Product: request to add a canary gating metric for RLHF workload types (95/99) before future kernel rollouts.
- Grace: coordinate customer follow-up; Laura can you send the updated note?

Attaching p99-graphs-rlhf-20260829.png and candidate-kernel-change.patch (for the engineering review).

Ben
SRE Manager

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-incident update: RLHF throughput dip (BrightCart) — actions and roadmap asks

Hi Jane / BrightCart Ops team (cc internal),

Thanks for the patience this morning. Summary and actions:

What happened (tl;dr):
- A recent kernel scheduling change (v4) increased overhead for long-sequence RLHF runs which surfaced as a throughput dip for GenAPI RLHF workloads.

Immediate actions taken:
- Targeted rollback of kernel-sched v4 across affected hosts (completed 09:50 PST).
- Temporary routing rule applied while monitoring stabilized.
- No additional customer data was exposed; this was an infra performance regression only.

Customer impact:
- BrightCart experienced elevated p99 for ~45 minutes; services are back to baseline. We are offering a one-time service credit for the affected window pending legal/billing approval.

Next steps (internal):
- ENG: full RCA and patch plan for kernel-sched v4 (owner: Marcus Lin).
- SRE: add automated canary gates to rollout pipeline for RLHF-like job classes (owner: Ben Carter).
- Product/CS: finalize customer-facing post-incident report and proposed credit (owner: Laura Bennett / Marissa Cole).

Roadmap asks (product):
- Prioritize a rollout gating feature that evaluates 95/99 latency on a per-workload basis before promoting runtime kernel updates.
- Consider runtime-level heuristics that detect long-sequence RLHF jobs and prefer stable kernels or increased KV-cache partitioning.

Customer note we sent (short):
Hi Jane — we’ve completed mitigation and rolled back the kernel change that caused the regression. Performance has returned to baseline. We’ll share a full RCA within 72 hours and propose a service credit for the impact window.

If BrightCart would like a 15-min post-mortem, we’re happy to schedule one.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
